nodes.description: Enamel is a secreted, protein-templated mineralized matrix, and it is the tissue in which SLC10A7 loss is most consistently expressed clinically. Slc10a7 is transcribed in the inner dental epithelium and in ameloblasts and odontoblasts during tooth development, mutant mice have tooth enamel anomalies, and every reported affected individual has amelogenesis imperfecta, typed as hypomineralized in the founding cohort and as hypoplastic/hypomineralized in the mildest case. Notably the founding study argued that the enamel phenotype is probably not explained by the proteoglycan defect alone, since amelogenesis imperfecta is what separates SSASKS from the other chondrodysplasias with multiple dislocations; the glycoprotein-trafficking arm is the more likely route.

nodes.description: SLC10A7 encodes a ten-transmembrane-domain protein of the SLC10 sodium/bile-acid cotransporter family which, unlike its relatives, transports none of the family's canonical substrates and remains an orphan carrier. It localizes to compartments of the secretory pathway, including the Golgi and the plasma membrane. Of the alleles actually assayed for protein level, a splice variant and the p.Leu74Pro missense reduce SLC10A7 protein expression; this is not a property of every missense allele, since p.Pro303Leu fibroblasts instead show SLC10A7 overexpression while the protein retains only partial calcium-regulatory activity. Hypomorphic rather than null function is the molecular basis of the milder end of the phenotypic spectrum. This is the disorder-specific lesion this entry substitutes for the generic Golgi trigger of the conserved CDG module.

nodes.description: Three glycosylation outputs fail together, which is why SSASKS is classified as a congenital disorder of glycosylation affecting multiple pathways rather than a single-enzyme defect. Heparan sulfate on proteoglycans is reduced roughly two-fold in patient fibroblasts and about 2.5-fold in mutant mouse cartilage, while total glycosaminoglycan content is preserved; N-glycans on plasma glycoproteins are abnormal; and O-GalNAc glycosylation is disrupted, with altered abundance of the C1GALT1 chaperone COSMC and mislocalization of the calcium-binding Golgi cargo sorter Cab45. This is the organ-agnostic substitution this entry makes against the CDG module's Golgi trigger: the module's generic disruption of Golgi glycosylation machinery is here caused by a luminal ionic lesion rather than by loss of a glycosyltransferase or of a tethering complex.

nodes.description: In the growth plate the consequence is architectural: mutant mice show shortened long bones with growth plate disorganization, and the human counterpart is disproportionate short stature with short long bones, small epiphyses and advanced carpal and tarsal ossification. Mineralization is reduced as well as growth: affected individuals have decreased bone mineral density compatible with osteoporosis, and knockdown zebrafish show a strong reduction in bone mineralization by alizarin red staining. This entry does not declare conformance to the defective_skeletal_mineralization module, because none of that module's three trigger arms (calciopenic, phosphopenic, mineralization-inhibitor excess) applies here — the lesion is failure to deliver the organic matrix, with normal calcium, phosphate and pyrophosphate handling as far as is reported.

nodes.description: SLC10A7 is a negative regulator of intracellular calcium signalling, and has been proposed to be renamed RCAS on that basis. Its expression is inversely correlated with store-operated calcium entry, and it co-localizes with STIM1, Orai1 and SERCA2. Loss of function therefore raises calcium influx: SLC10A7 knockout cells show increased influx after thapsigargin, ionomycin and ATP/carbachol, and patient fibroblasts show increased Ca2+ influx after an extracellular calcium challenge. Within the secretory pathway itself the consequence is an increased ER and Golgi calcium content. Because Golgi glycosyltransferase activity and Golgi organization are calcium-dependent, this node is the rate-limiting step linking an orphan transporter to a glycosylation disease.
